summary:
Iteration 154 — Backend-only verification of the rendered
HTML appended to body by GET /api/news/articles/{id}. Created /app/backend/tests/test_liveblog_body_html.py with 8 pytest cases covering every review-request scenario: (1) full structure with 2 published entries — exactly one
, one
    , 2
  1. , with Dutch-formatted label containing ' · ' and a Dutch month name, h3 only when title is set,
critical_code_review_comments: news_public._render_liveblog_html correctly escapes title via _html.escape but body is passed through verbatim — relies on TinyMCE sanitisation upstream; if a non-TinyMCE client (API import) ever posts raw <script> in entry.body the timeline will inject it. Worth adding a server-side sanitiser (bleach) before append, even if low risk.

_render_liveblog_html prints video.embed_html unsanitised — same XSS surface as above. embed_html is generated by services.video_embed for trusted providers, but if any UI path ever lets editors paste raw HTML into that field, we'd leak it. Consider whitelisting iframe src.

Header text 'Liveblog beëindigd' uses the Dutch ë — must be served as UTF-8. The FastAPI default JSONResponse handles this fine, but if any downstream consumer (grk.fm) reads the body without explicit utf-8 it will mojibake. Spec-compliant today.
_format_entry_datetime_nl falls back to str(ts) on parse failure — could surface a raw timezone-aware ISO in the user-facing <time> label. Minor; would only show on a corrupt timestamp.

auto-archive helper _maybe_archive_liveblog runs on every GET — adds a Mongo write on the hot path. Fine for now (only fires when 6h has elapsed) but consider gating with an in-memory TTL cache if traffic grows.

The body HTML is concatenated as a string (out['body'] + timeline_html) — fine, but means consumers wanting to insert anything BETWEEN body and the timeline can't. If grk.fm ever wants e.g. a related-articles widget between the two, we'd need a separate field.
seed_data_creation: Each test creates its own TEST_LBHTML_* content_item (via POST /api/content + PUT is_liveblog=true) and force-publishes it directly in Mongo (status=published, approval_status=approved). Module-scoped cleanup fixture tracks every created article id and tears down all liveblog_entries + content_items at session end.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Two regression suites now cover the liveblog feature end-to-end: /app/backend/tests/test_liveblog_publish_flow.py (auto-publish + visibility) and /app/backend/tests/test_liveblog_body_html.py (HTML rendering). Re-run with: cd /app/backend && pytest tests/test_liveblog_body_html.py tests/test_liveblog_publish_flow.py -v. Helper pattern: create an article via /api/content then force status=published + approval_status=approved directly in Mongo (publish-clara requires a featured image with rights, which we don't want to upload in tests).
rca of the issue:
Original bug: grk.fm only rendered the `body` HTML field from the public News API. The liveblog_entries[] JSON array was present but never read, so published entries were invisible to readers. Fix verified: _render_liveblog_html builds a self-contained
...
  1. ... timeline and get_article_detail appends it to body BEFORE returning. The liveblog_entries[] array stays in the response for clients that prefer to render their own UI. Featured-image caption injection and inline figcaption wrapping (existing behaviour) remain intact and execute BEFORE the timeline is appended, so they sit at the top of body.
